01 / THE PERSON

From building technology
to leading the business.

Before the CEO title came more than two decades inside Microsoft. Nadella joined in 1992 and went on to lead its Cloud and Enterprise group before taking the top job in February 2014.

His background combines electrical engineering, computer science, and business. Originally from Hyderabad, India, he worked at Sun Microsystems before Microsoft.

That path gives this profile its central question: how does a leader carry an engineer’s perspective into decisions about an entire company?

Source: Microsoft leadership biography

03 / PIVOTAL MOMENTS

The turns that changed the story.

  1. 1992

    The move to Microsoft

    Joins Microsoft after working at Sun Microsystems. It becomes the company where he builds his executive career.

    Read the source
  2. 2014

    From cloud leader to CEO

    Appointed chief executive on February 4, after leading the Cloud and Enterprise group.

    Read the source
  3. 2016

    A bet on the professional network

    Microsoft completes its LinkedIn acquisition on December 8, adding a major professional network to its business.

    Read the source
  4. 2019

    The OpenAI partnership begins

    Microsoft announces a $1B investment and a computing partnership focused on large-scale AI.

    Read the source
  5. 2021

    The board-chair role

    Independent directors elect him chair on June 16, adding board leadership to the CEO position.

    Read the source

07 / THE CONVERSATIONINTERVIEW AGENDA

The questions we’d ask.

An editorial agenda for a future conversation. These are proposed questions, not an interview or statements attributed to Nadella.

  1. 01

    How do you decide what deserves a decade of investment?

    On balancing the next platform with the demands of the current business.

  2. 02

    What changes when AI becomes part of everyone’s job?

    On skills, responsibility, and the relationship between people and their tools.

  3. 03

    What do you still approach as an engineer?

    On the habits that survive the move from building products to leading a company.
